key_insight: The lead-free double perovskites K2SnGeX6 and Rb2SnGeX6 are predicted by DFT to be stable, ductile, and strongly tunable in bandgap and thermoelectric performance by changing halogen composition.
engineering_relevance: These materials could support safer photovoltaic absorbers, tandem/infrared optoelectronics, and high-temperature waste-heat recovery with reduced toxic lead content.
method: Density functional theory across K/Rb and Cl/Br/I compositions
Stability screening using formation energy, tolerance factor, and octahedral factor
Property analysis of elastic, electronic, optical, and thermoelectric behavior
evidence_signal: The abstract reports all six compounds as thermodynamically stable cubic phases, direct bandgaps tunable from 1.44 to 0.64 eV, and a peak predicted ZT of 2.4 for K2SnGeI6 at 1000 K.
watch_item: Results are theoretical and depend on DFT approximations, so experimental synthesis, defect tolerance, and device-level stability still need validation.
paper_title: First-Principles Study of Novel Lead-Free Double Perovskite \b{eta}2SnGeX6 (\b{eta} = K, Rb; X = Cl, Br, I) for thermomechanical, optoelectronic and outstanding thermoelectric applications
